Advanced Vision Control

Vision wins objectives. Learn when to set up before Dragon and Baron, how to sweep, where to deep ward, how to use Faelights, and how to deny the enemy's sight.

Vision is about information and denial

In Vision Basics: Wards and the Minimap you learned to place wards so you don't get ganked. At a higher level, vision is a fight for information. The team that sees more makes better decisions: they know when to start Baron, when to fight, and when to run.

That means two jobs: getting vision for your team, and denying vision from the enemy. Removing enemy wards is often worth more than placing yours.

Your tools right now:

  • Up to 3 Stealth Wards and 1 Control Ward on the map per player. You can carry two Control Wards at 75 gold each (supports pay 40 after their quest).
  • Oracle Lens: the red trinket that reveals and disables wards around you for 8 seconds.
  • Farsight Alteration: the blue trinket that places a visible, permanent ward from very far away.
  • Faelights: glowing mushroom rings on the map. A ward placed on one becomes a superward with 25% more sight and extra vision of the nearby area for 45 seconds.

Set up 60-90 seconds before an objective

The most common reason teams lose Dragon or Baron is that they show up at the last second. The enemy already has wards around the pit and sees everything you do.

Use this timeline, using the timers on our Objective Timers page:

  1. 90 seconds before: push your mid wave and the side wave closest to the objective. You need minion pressure so the enemy has to deal with waves while you set up.
  2. 60 seconds before: your jungler and support walk in with Oracle Lens and Control Wards. Sweep the entrances to the pit and place your own wards in the bushes the enemy will walk through.
  3. 30 seconds before: the rest of the team arrives. Place a Control Ward in or next to the pit so the enemy can't ward it at the last second.

Around Dragon and Baron, the river bushes across from the pits have Faelights. Warding one gives you a huge view of how the enemy will approach.

Pro tipThe side that has priority (pushed waves) gets to set vision first. That's why winning lanes before an objective spawns matters so much.

Sweeping well

Oracle Lens only lasts 8 seconds, so don't waste it. Use it where wards are most likely to be: bush entrances to your jungle, the river bushes near objectives, and the spot where you just saw an enemy support walk.

Habits that help:

  • Swap to Oracle Lens once your support or jungler role starts setting up objectives, and many mid laners do the same after the first few recalls.
  • Buy a Control Ward every time you recall if you have a free slot. It's the best 75 gold in the game.
  • Place your Control Ward where it's hard to find and useful for a long time, like the inside corner of a bush, so the enemy can't easily clear it.

The rune Sixth Sense (Domination) automatically finds a nearby enemy ward every so often, and at level 11 reveals it. Some supports and junglers use it to win the vision war.

Common mistakePlacing a Control Ward in the open river where the enemy will see and destroy it for free. A ward that lives 10 seconds gives the enemy gold and you nothing.

Deep wards and tracking

A deep ward is a ward placed in the enemy's jungle, near their buffs or the paths they use. It tells you where the enemy jungler is starting, when they go for a buff, and when their team rotates.

Good deep ward spots when you're ahead:

  • The enemy's blue or red buff, about 30 seconds before it respawns.
  • The bush that connects the enemy jungle to their side lane, so your split pusher sees enemies coming.
  • The enemy raptor area, which many junglers path through.

The Deep Ward rune makes your wards in the enemy jungle tougher and longer-lasting. When you're behind, don't deep ward: it's too dangerous. Ward your own jungle instead, so you see invades coming.

Vision lines for sieging and defending

When you push a turret as a team, think of a vision line: a row of wards across the enemy jungle entrances near that lane. It tells you if someone tries to flank or walk around behind you.

When defending, do the opposite. Clear the enemy's wards near your turret with Oracle Lens, then stand in the fog. If the enemy can't see you, they don't know if it's safe to dive, and they'll often wait too long.

A clear pattern: take a turret, then immediately ward deeper in that part of the enemy jungle. Each turret you take opens more of the map to safe vision.

Denying vision wins fights before they start

If the enemy can't see your team, they have to guess. Teams that guess make mistakes: they face-check bushes, start Baron when you're right there, or fight with only four players.

Before a big objective, try to have the enemy see nothing on your half of the river. Then you can stand in an unexpected spot, wait for them to walk in, and start the fight on your terms.

Track how many wards the enemy places. If their support recalls and comes back with Control Wards, expect new vision near the next objective, and sweep again.

Key takeaways

  • Arrive at objectives 60-90 seconds early, after pushing nearby waves.
  • Each player can have 3 Stealth Wards and 1 Control Ward placed; buy Control Wards every recall.
  • Use Faelights near Dragon and Baron for a 45-second superward.
  • Deep ward when ahead, ward your own jungle when behind.
  • Denying enemy vision is often worth more than placing your own.
